WITHOUT IMPOSING ANY TOLLS, IN LINE WITH THE OUTCOMES 
AND EFFORTS REACHED BY THE UNITED STATES AND ISLAMIC 
REPUBLIC OF IRAN.
2. THE SULTANATE OF OMAN HAS WORKED IN COORDINATION WITH
THE INTERNATIONAL MARITIME ORGANIZATION (IMO) TO PROVIDE
ALL VESSELS WITH THE OPTION OF A TEMPORARY MARITIME 
CORRIDOR DEFINED BY THE COORDINATES LISTED BELOW.
3. THE SAFETY OF NAVIGATION REMAINS THE PARAMOUNT CONSIDERATION.
GIVEN THE ELEVATED RISK OF COLLISION IN THE CURRENT ENVIRONMENT,
A GRADUAL AND CONTROLLED EVACUATION OF VESSEL TRAFFIC IS REQUIRED.
4. TO MITIGATE THESE RISKS, THE IMO HAS DEVELOPED A PHASED 
APPROACH BASED ON GROUPS OF VESSELS WITH THE FULL COORDINATION
OF THE OMANI AUTHORITIES.
5. CURRENT REPORTS INDICATE THAT THE TSS IS NOT SAFE FOR USE AT
THIS TIME. BASED ON AVAILABLE INFORMATION FROM THE IMO, TWO 
TEMPORARY ROUTES MAY BE UTILIZED BY VESSELS DEPARTING THROUGH
THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ: ONE SOUTH OF THE EXISTING TRAFFIC 
SEPARATION SCHEME (TSS) AND ONE TO THE NORTH.
6. VESSELS INCLUDED IN THE DESIGNATED GROUPS WILL BE CONTACTED 
INDIVIDUALLY AND PROVIDED WITH FURTHER INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING 
THEIR DEPARTURE BY RELEVANT PARTIES COORDINATED BY THE IMO.

AND ADVISED OF THEIR ALLOCATED TRANSIT DAY BY THE PARTIES COORDINATED
BY IMO.

THE DESIGNATED WAITING AREA WITHIN INTERNATIONAL WATERS, 
WITHIN A 3 NM RADIUS OF POSITION 26-16.17N/055-46.52E.

In de volgende gebieden op de Westerschelde zijn locaties aangewezen voor het gebruik van spudpalen: 5.1.1. Vaarwater langs Hoofdplaat 5.1.2. Everingen Zuid zijde 5.1.3. Middelgat 5.1.4. Voorschriften voor gebruik van ankergebieden Westerschelde en haar mondingen 6.1. Alle vaartuigen mogen pas ankeren na verkregen toestemming van de GNA. De toestemming kan door de GNA via de desbetreffende verkeerscentrale worden gegeven. Aan de toestemming kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden. 6.2. Voorschriften van toepassing op alle schepen: a. Binnen de begrenzing van de ankergebieden Westhinder, Oostdyck en Schouwenbank kan zelf een ankerplaats worden gekozen. Voordat het schip het anker laat vallen, zal de positie moeten worden goedgekeurd door de desbetreffende verkeerscentrale. b. In ankergebieden Wielingen Noord, Wielingen Zuid en Vlissingen Rede is het ten anker liggen onder normale omstandigheden gelimiteerd tot maximaal 24 uur. c. Voor werkzaamheden op de ankerplaatsen dient toestemming en/of een vergunning te worden aangevraagd volgens onderstaande methoden: 1) Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale voor de ankergebieden Westhinder, Oostdyck en Schouwenbank. 2) Via het havensysteem Enigma+ voor de Everingen positie A t/m E en de Put van Terneuzen positie A en B. 3) Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale in de gebieden voor overslag werkzaamheden van zand en grind. Dit staat beschreven in artikel 10 van deze GB. 4) Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale of per email via de GNA voor de nog niet benoemde gebieden in dit artikel. d. Het is verboden om spudpalen te gebruiken in de aangewezen ankergebieden, tenzij het ankergebied tevens is aangewezen als gebied voor het gebruik van spudpalen. 6.3. Voorschriften van toepassing op gastankers of geladen met gevaarlijke stoffen: a. Voor gastankers waarop de GB “Vervoer van gevaarlijke stoffen in gastankers binnen het GNB- gebied” van toepassing is geldt het volgende indien de reis van een Vaarplan IMO 2 Gastanker om enige reden zou moeten worden onderbroken: 1) Het schip moet ten anker komen op een door de GNA aangewezen ankerplaats. 2) Voor een schip met bestemming of komend van Zeebrugge zal een aanbevolen ankerplaats worden toegewezen. Indien er een loods aan boord is wordt de ankerplaats toegewezen door de VC Zeebrugge in samenspraak met de GNA en de bedienende loods. Indien er geen loods aan boord is wijst VC Zeebrugge het ankergebied Westhinder aan. 3) Voor een schip met een andere bestemming binnen het GNB-gebied zal deze ten anker komen in een bij voorkeur zo westelijk mogelijke positie in ankergebied Wielingen Noord of indien beschikbaar ankerplaats Everingen Alfa. b. Schepen die geladen zijn met gevaarlijke stoffen genoemd in bijlage 1 van het SRW mogen enkel ankeren in de ankergebieden Westhinder en Schouwenbank. In geval van overmacht kan er met toestemming van de GNA zo westelijk mogelijk geankerd worden in ankergebied Wielingen Noord. c. Schepen met een lengte ≤ 110 m die geladen zijn met gevaarlijke stoffen genoemd in bijlage 1 van het SRW (niet zijnde gevaarlijke stoffen genoemd onder SRW bijlage 1, lid 1 en 2), mogen met toestemming van de GNA ankeren in ankergebied Vlissingen Rede oostelijk deel (‘driehoek’). Dit enkel in geval van bezwaren van nautische of meteorologische aard. Artikel 7. Voorschriften voor gebruik van ankergebieden Beneden-Zeeschelde 7.1. Aan de toestemming kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden. 7.2. De GNA bepaalt de locatie waar en de voorwaarden waaronder een vaartuig kan ankeren. 7.3. Voor werkzaamheden op de ankerplaatsen dient toestemming en/of een vergunning te worden aangevraagd volgens onderstaande methoden: a. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale of per email via de GNA. b. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale in de gebieden voor overslag werkzaamheden van zand en grind. Dit staat beschreven in artikel 10 van deze GB. 7.4. Het is verboden om spudpalen te gebruiken in de aangewezen ankergebieden, tenzij het ankergebied tevens is aangewezen als gebied voor het gebruik van spudpalen. Artikel 8. Voorschriften voor gebruik van spudpalen in de aangewezen gebieden op de Westerschelde en Beneden-Zeeschelde 8.1. Alle vaartuigen mogen gebruik maken van hun spudpalen na verkregen toestemming van de GNA. Aan de toestemming kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden. 8.2. De GNA bepaalt de locatie waar en de voorwaarden waaronder een vaartuig gebruik kan maken van spudpalen. 8.3. Wanneer het desbetreffende schip op haar spudpalen ligt wordt dit gemeld aan de desbetreffende verkeerscentrale. 8.4. Niets ontheft hierbij de gezagvoerder van het lopen van ankerwacht conform de huidige wet- en regelgeving. Daarbij is het verplicht om te alle tijden uit te luisteren op het juiste VHF verkeerskanaal. 8.5. Voor werkzaamheden in de aangewezen gebieden voor het gebruik van spudpalen dient toestemming en/of een vergunning te worden aangevraagd volgens onderstaande methoden: a. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale of per email via de GNA. b. Per marifoon via de betreffende verkeerscentrale in de gebieden voor overslag werkzaamheden van zand en grind. Dit staat beschreven in artikel 10 van deze GB. Artikel 9. Ankeren van schepen met schade na een incident 9.1. Schepen die na een incident schade of vermoedelijke schade hebben opgelopen mogen hun reis naar hun eindbestemming slechts voortzetten na toestemming van de GNA. 9.2. De schepen dienen in principe eerst ten anker te komen op een door de GNA aangewezen ankerplaats alwaar een eerste onderzoek naar de aard van de schade wordt uitgevoerd. 9.3. Bij een incident moet onderstaande wetgeving in acht worden genomen: - KB houdende politie- en scheepvaartreglement voor de Belgische territoriale zee, de havens en de stranden van de Belgische kust (1981), artikel 27 en 29. - KB houdende scheepvaartreglement voor de Beneden-Zeeschelde (1992), artikel 44 en 47. - Scheepvaartreglement Westerschelde 1990, artikel 51 en 54. - Scheepvaartreglement voor het Kanaal van Gent naar Terneuzen, artikel 43 en 53. - KB houdende Scheepvaartreglement voor het Kanaal van Gent naar Terneuzen (1992), artikel 43 en 52. - Havenpolitieverordening Haven van Antwerpen (2024), artikel 8.1.4 lid 1. - Havenverordening North Sea Port 2025 (Gemeente Vlissingen, Borsele en Terneuzen), artikel 3.9. - Havenpolitieverordening North Sea Port Gent (2026), artikel 3.2.1. Artikel 10. Overslag van zeezand en grind 10.1. De overslag van zeezand en grind is enkel toegestaan op de door de GNA aangewezen gebieden en onder bepaalde voorwaarden. Dit wordt nader geregeld middels een GB (of een Bass). Artikel 11. Bijzondere omstandigheden en uitzonderingen 11.1. Afhankelijk van de omstandigheden, technische mogelijkheden, scheepstypen, soort lading of verkeerssituatie kan de Gemeenschappelijke Nautische Autoriteit extra voorschriften vaststellen dan wel afwijken en/of uitzonderingen maken van/op deze voorschriften. 1.The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) notes in past marine incidents the need for crew familiarization with shipboard equipment and systems.
2.This Marine Notice wishes to make recommendations to all Shipowners & operators having large fleets for the need to establish dedicated onshore or fleet-based training workshops specifically for crew trainings and practices. These workshops will boost crew familiarity, hands-on safety drill practice, and operational readiness for onboard equipment and systems.
3.Be advised that the Maritime Transport Act 2013 and the Maritime (STCW Convention) Regulations 2014 highlights the need for crew familiarization with critical shipboard equipment, bridge systems, safety gear, and emergency appliances through continuous practical training as it would enhance maritime safety and the protection of the marine environment.
4.For any clarification, please contact the undersigned.
SAVENACA CAVALEVU
EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN (MSAF)
Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji
22nd October 2026

1.This Marine Notice serves to remind all Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents of the importance of maintaining order and discipline of all persons on board ships to protect safety of life at sea and ensure lawful crew management.
2.With recent cases on the above subject matter, the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) would like to remind all Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents of the Master’s duty to have the final authority to control the ship while in command and for the discipline of all persons on board.
3.Additionally, Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents are reminded to ensure that disciplinary procedures are implemented as part of the Safe Ship Management System for the Company and also onboard its ships.
4.This Notice serves to give notice that any misconduct affecting the safe operation of the ships, repeated disregard of lawful safety requirements or instructions, or misconduct contributing to any accident, incident or mishap should be reported to the MSAF. Any such recurring records against a seafarer will engage the enforcement measures of MSAF.

The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) wishes to advise all shipowners, ship operators, Masters and Maritime stakeholders of the servicing facility currently approved by the Authority to undertake the servicing of inflatable liferafts in Fiji.
This Marine Notice is issued to ensure that inflatable liferafts carried on vessels are serviced by an MSAF-approved servicing station and within the approved scope of the facility.
Approved Liferaft Servicing Station
Facility: Liferaft Sales and Service Centre (Fiji) Pte Limited.
Location: Corner of Renown Street and Rodwell Road, Suva.
MSAF Statement of Compliance: LRSC 01/2026.
The facility has been assessed and approved by MSAF in accordance with regulation 10.4 Paragraph 10 of the Maritime (Fiji Maritime Code) Regulations 2014.

The specific Liferaft types and models covered by the facility approval are provided in Appendix A to this Marine Notice.
Advice to Shipowners and Operators
•Ensure liferaft are serviced at the required intervals.
•Ensure servicing is undertaken by an MSAF-approved servicing station.
•Confirm that the servicing station is authorised to service the particular make, type and model of liferaft presented.
•Retain servicing documentation and make it available during MSAF surveys and inspections.
•Do not accept servicing or certification of liferaft that fall outside the approved scope of the servicing station.
Where a liferaft make or model is not listed in Appendix A, shipowners and operators are advised to contact MSAF before making servicing arrangements. MSAF will advise the maritime industry through appropriate notices should additional servicing stations or liferaft brands be approved.

w.id: Hong Kong Coastal Hong Kong MDN 214/2026
w.t:
MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 214/2026 (Navigation Warnings & Related Information)
Cross Harbour Swimming Races and Closure of Landing Steps
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that swimming races across the Central Harbour from Wan Chai, Hong Kong Island to Tsim Sha Tsui, Kowloon will take place from 0700 hours to 1100 hours on 15 November 2026. About 4,000 swimmers, under the escort of guard boats, are expected to participate in the races.
2. Launches of the Marine Department and Marine Police will be stationed or patrolling in the Central Harbour before and during the event.
3. Masters, coxswains and persons-in-charge of all vessels navigating in the vicinity should proceed with caution and give a wide berth to the swimmers, and follow the directions given by officers on Marine Department and Marine Police launches regulating marine traffic in the vicinity.
4. As the marine traffic in the Central Harbour will be affected by the races, vessel operators are advised to adjust their sailing schedules in order to avoid obstructing the races.
5. To facilitate the event, the following landing steps will be temporarily closed:
(i) Public Landings at the starting/finishing points – from 0900 hours on 14 November 2026 to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026;
(ii) Kowloon Public Pier No. 1 – from 0900 hours on 14 November 2026 to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026; and
(iii) Kowloon Public Pier No. 2 to No. 4 – from 0500 hours to 1300 hours on 15 November 2026.
6. During the aforementioned closure periods, owners and coxswains of vessels are advised to use other landing facilities in the vicinity.
7. A drawing showing the route of the races and the affected landing step is attached to this Notice.
Mr. S.F. WONG Director of Marine
Marine Department Government of the HKSAR Date: 10 November 2026 Action File Ref.: L/M 704/26 in MD-HPS-F01-015-045-002

w.t:
MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 85/2026 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring “B” mooring A17, A29, A35, B2, B4 A36, A38, A39, A43, A78
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. Further information on minimum safe manning levels on ships while in the waters of Hong Kong can be found in Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/proc/index.html)
8. Coxswains, owners, agents and persons in control of local vessels are advised to take the precautionary measures contained in the Marine Department pamphlet entitled “Measures to Enhance the Safety of Local Vessels During Passage of Tropical Cyclones” well before a tropical cyclone is approaching Hong Kong. The pamphlet is available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/publication/materials/pdf/hps_cyclones.pdf)
9. This Notice supersedes Marine Department Notice No. 60 of 2025.
Mr. S.F. WONG Director of Marine

MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 41/2026 (Marine Works)
Improvement Works at Yung Shue O Jetty
With immediate effect and for a period of approximately 21 months, improvement works for the jetty will be carried out within the area bounded by straight lines joining the following co-ordinates (WGS 84 Datum) from (A) to (F) and the adjacent shoreline:
(A) 22-25.17N 114-16.65E (B) 22-25.18N 114-16.62E (C) 22-25.21N 114-16.64E (D) 22-25.20N 114-16.65E (E) 22-25.23N 114-16.67E (F) 22-25.20N 114-16.72E
2. The works will be carried out by two dumb lighters and one pilling barge. One roro barge, one tugboat and one work boat will provide assistance. Vessels engaged in the works will display signals as prescribed in international and local regulations.
3. The hours of work will be from 0700 to 1900 hours. No works will be carried out on Sundays and public holidays. Vessels employed for the works will stay in the works area outside the hours of work.
4. A working area of approximately 20 metres around the working vessels will be established. Yellow marker buoys fitted with yellow flashing lights will be laid to mark the positions of the anchors extending from the working vessels.
5. Silt curtains, which are large pieces of netting to contain mud and sediments extending from the sea surface to the seabed, will be established within the works area. Yellow marker buoys fitted with yellow flashing lights will be laid to mark the extent of the silt curtains.
6. Diving operations will be carried out from time to time during the hours of work. Vessels navigating in the vicinity should proceed with caution and keep clear of the works area at slow speed, bearing in mind that there are divers working in the area.
7. A drawing showing the works area is attached to this Notice.
Mr. S.F. WONG Director of Marine

w.t:
MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 60/2025 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring “B” mooring A17, A36, A43 B03, B04 A74, A77
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. MARINE DEPARTMENT NOTICE NO. 71/2024 (Navigational Warnings and Related Information)
Typhoon Season
Owners, agents and charterers are requested to remind their ship masters of the need to take precautionary measures during the approach of tropical cyclones.
2. Masters and persons in control of vessels should closely monitor the development of tropical cyclones for making early preparation. This includes carrying out thorough inspections on board to ensure that the engines, mooring gears and other safety equipment of vessels are in good working conditions. When safe and practicable, consideration should be given to arrange vessels to leave the berth in ample time and proceed outside Hong Kong waters for shelter from extreme weather associated with super typhoons.
3. Masters, owners, agents and persons in control of vessels are also reminded of their obligation to comply with any direction issued by the Director of Marine concerning the safe operation of vessels and the port, or in relation to any matter which the Director may give directions under the laws of Hong Kong.
4. When a tropical cyclone warning is issued by the Hong Kong Observatory, every vessel which is moored to the following government mooring buoys shall clear anchors and cables and prepares the main propulsion machinery to full power condition. Such vessel shall, if so directed by the Director, leave the mooring buoy-
“A” mooring
“B” mooring A17, A36, A73 B03, B30 A74, A77, A78
Other details of government mooring buoys are available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/moor/index.html)
5. The master of a ship moored to a government mooring buoy may, at his discretion, drop a bow anchor under foot to lessen the tendency to sheer. This should not impair the efficiency of the mooring, although an anchor should not be used during normal weather conditions.
6. Masters are reminded that every vessel within the waters of Hong Kong must maintain continuous listening watch on the VHF radio channel appropriate to the VHF sector in which the vessel is located, or another VHF channel as may be specified by the Vessel Traffic Centre (call sign “MARDEP”). The Centre will broadcast tropical cyclone information from time to time when tropical cyclone warning signals have been issued. Masters should also listen to local radio broadcasts for weather advisory information bulletins.
7. An inadequately manned vessel during the passage of a tropical cyclone not only places itself at risk but also endangers the port and other vessels. Masters, owners, agents, and charterers of vessels should therefore ensure that sufficient number of qualified crew capable of carrying out all duties to ensure the safety of ship having regard to the pertaining circumstances are on board at all times during the passage of a tropical cyclone. Further information on minimum safe manning levels on ships while in the waters of Hong Kong can be found in Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/public-services/port-services/proc/index.html)
8. Coxswains, owners, agents and persons in control of local vessels are advised to take the precautionary measures contained in the Marine Department pamphlet entitled “Measures to Enhance the Safety of Local Vessels During Passage of Tropical Cyclones” well before a tropical cyclone is approaching Hong Kong. The pamphlet is available on the Marine Department’s website. (https://www.mardep.gov.hk/en/publication/materials/pdf/hps_cyclones.pdf)
9. This Notice supersedes Marine Department Notice No. 77 of 2023.

Due to the existing risks along the current Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS) in the Strait of Hormuz, and 
to ensure secure and safe of navigation in this important waterway, the Sultanate of Oman in 
coordination with the IMO, has issued important guidance and instructions for vessels planning to transit 
the Strait without the imposition of any tolls.

Effective 241500 UTC Oct 2026, the following North Atlantic Right Whale restriction Zones are in effect for all vessels greater than 13 meters in length overall:
Static Zones North and South: Vessels must not exceed 10 knots over ground.
Dynamic Shipping Zones A, B, C, D, and E: No restriction in effect.
Seasonal Management Areas 1 and 2: No restriction in effect.
Restricted area: No restriction in effect.
Voluntary Seasonal Slowdown: Vessels are requested to reduce their speed less than 10 knots over ground.
Additional details are available in Notices to Mariners. Failure to comply with speed restrictions in effect can lead to enforcement action by Transport Canada.
Mariners are requested to report whale sightings and observations of entangled, dead, or injured whales to Marine Communication and Traffic Services.

HARO STRAIT AND BOUNDARY PASS – ECHO Program 2025 Voluntary Ship Slowdown
Effective June 15 to November 30, 2026 the ECHO Program voluntary ship slowdown through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass is active for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales. This initiative will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PDT on November 30, 2026, depending on southern resident killer whale presence in the fall. If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water:
11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and,
14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels.
This voluntary slowdown takes place between the vessel traffic separation scheme at the south end of Haro Strait at 48-24-22.78 N ,123-12-15.26 W, and the vessel traffic separation scheme at the north end of Boundary Pass at 48-46-39.28 N, 123-1-36.84 W. There are also two optional slow down areas, one rounding Turn Point and the other between Saturna Island and Alden Point, Patos Island.
The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups.
For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address:
https://www.portvancouver.com/echo/

Effective 0700 UTC JUN 1 2026, to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of Southern Resident Killer Whales (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026, vessels must not approach within a distance of 1000m of a Southern Resident Killer Whale in the Southern Resident Killer Whale critical habitat and British Columbia coastal waters east of Vancouver Island and south of Campbell River (Cape Mudge) and Ucluelet, including Barkley Sound (up to Port Alberni) and Howe Sound, with coordinates listed in Schedule 1 of the Interim Order.
These prohibitions are in effect until May 31st, 2027. Details of vessel exceptions from the approach distance are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 3(2), and 4(2) of the Interim Order. Note that vessels in transit are excepted from the approach distance measure.
Vessels must not operate or navigate within the two Vessel Restricted Zones, specifically those waters off the eastern coast of Saturna Island and southern coast of North Pender Island, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 2 of the Interim Order.
The Vessel Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Vessel Restricted Zone prohibitions are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 5(2) and 6(2) of the Interim Order.
In addition, vessels must adhere to the requirements of two Speed Restricted Zones near Swiftsure Bank, in which all vessels are restricted to a maximum speed of 10 knots over ground, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 3 of the Interim Order.
The Speed Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Speed Restricted Zones are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 7(2) and 8(2) of the Interim Order.
Failure to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whales in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 could lead to enforcement action, including fines.
Further details are available at Transport Canada’s website (Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whale (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 (canada.ca), or upon request from a Marine Communications and Traffic Services Centre.

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-42-2026 November 9, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Increase in the Number of Booking Slots at the Panamax Locks and in the Maximum Allowable Draft at the Neopanamax Locks Supported by improving water conditions, favorable hydrological projections, and the effectiveness of the water-saving measures implemented at the locks, the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announces an additional booking slot at the Panamax Locks and an increase in the maximum allowable draft at the Neopanamax Locks. Effective immediately, the daily capacity for vessels in the Super category will increase from eighteen (18) to nineteen (19) slots. The additional slot will be offered as follows: through Booking Period 3 (Auction) for booking dates from November 12 to November 17, 2026; through Booking Period 2 (Special Competition) for booking dates from November 18 to 23, 2026, and for booking dates beginning November 24, 2026, at the opening of the 2nd Period Competition on November 10, 2026. With this adjustment, the total daily capacity will increase to 34 transit slots across the Neopanamax and Panamax Locks, providing customers greater access and planning flexibility. Under this update, first-transit vessels may participate in the NetZero Slot competition once the ACP has issued the required preliminary admeasurement inspection. 1. Requirements for First-Time Transit Vessels to Participate To participate in the NetZero Slot competition, first-time vessels must obtain a preliminary admeasurement inspection from the Panama Canal Admeasurement Unit prior to the competition date. This preliminary determination must include the following information needed to evaluate the vessel for the competition date: • Toll basis • Panama Canal Universal Measurement System (PC/UMS) tonnage • Review of all pertinent information for the vessel database, including the engine type and the vessel’s eligibility for the NetZero Program • Any other vessel information required by the ACP. 2. How Customers May Request a Preliminary Admeasurement Inspection Vessel owners, operators, or authorized vessel agents interested in participating in the NetZero Slot competition with first-time vessels may request a preliminary admeasurement determination through the Panama Canal Admeasurement Unit, in accordance with ACP-established procedures. Requests shall include the technical documentation and information required by the ACP and are subject to applicable fees and charges. Submission of a request does not, itself, establish eligibility. Eligibility will be confirmed only after the Panama Canal Admeasurement Unit has completed the required evaluation and issued the corresponding preliminary admeasurement inspection. 3. Admeasurement Review and Vessel Inspection The ACP may issue the preliminary admeasurement determination supported by the documents submitted and, when necessary, a vessel inspection. A vessel inspection may be conducted outside the Republic of Panama under Maritime Service Tariff Item 1080, Vessel Inspections Overseas, Subject to Customer Request. Modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announces modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System, including the reversal of a temporary measure introduced in July 2026 in response to changes in global shipping patterns that placed additional pressure on transit demand. As vessel traffic has since normalized, the ACP will return to the previous allocation criteria. Therefore, effective immediately, during Booking Periods 1A and 2 for the Neopanamax locks, any slot that is cancelled or otherwise becomes available will be allocated through a Special Competition using the following order of priority: Full Container, LNG, LPG, and Car Carrier/RoRo vessels. Within each vessel category, the first tiebreaker will be TTA, when applicable, followed by customer ranking as the second tiebreaker. While the water deficit in the Canal watershed persists, the Transit Reservation (Booking) System remains the only mechanism to guarantee a transit date. Therefore, vessels without a reservation may experience extremely extensive delays. The Canal remains committed to closely monitoring water conditions and rainfall levels and will communicate any further adjustments in a timely manner, as circumstances warrant. September 16, 2026. TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Clarification on Consecutive Booking Dates Limitation in the Panamax Locks Across Different Booking Periods
The Panama Canal Authority hereby clarifies the application of the booking eligibility rules related to consecutive booking dates in the Transit Reservation System for the Panamax Locks. This clarification is provided in connection with the provisions introduced through Advisory to Shipping No. A-28-2026 regarding booking slot eligibility across competitions and special competitions conducted in different booking periods. All other Panamax booking slot allocation rules published in Advisory to Shipping No. A- 28-2026 remain in effect and are not affected by this clarification.
Effective immediately, the restriction on obtaining booking slots for consecutive transit dates shall not apply when the bookings are awarded through different booking periods. This clarification applies exclusively to Panamax Locks.
Accordingly, a customer that has been awarded a booking slot for a transit date during Booking Period 1 may also participate in, and be awarded, a booking slot for the following transit date during Booking Period 2, subject to slot availability and compliance with all other applicable reservation process requirements.
This clarification is intended to ensure a consistent interpretation of the current rules, avoid unintended restrictions and provide customers with greater clarity and predictability when planning multiple transits.
Consequently, the consecutive booking date limitation shall apply only within the same booking period and shall not prevent customers from obtaining booking slots for consecutive transit dates when such slots are awarded through different booking periods.
For any further inquiries regarding these rules, please contact: operationservices@pancanal.com.

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations
Advisory to Shipping No. A-29-2026
August 20, 2026 TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Additional Measures to Address Reduced Precipitation in the Canal Watershed
Despite the arrival of the rainy season in the Isthmus of Panama and the water-saving measures implemented by the Panama Canal Authority (ACP) in recent months to mitigate the adverse effects of the El Niño event, current watershed conditions continue to warrant additional preventive measures to support the long-term sustainability of Canal operations. During the current hydrological year (May through August), cumulative rainfall across the Canal watershed has been 34% below the historical average, while watershed inflows have been 44% below their historical average for the same period, reflecting a substantially reduced hydrologic response despite the onset of the rainy season. Furthermore, forecasts indicate that the anticipated severity of the 2026-2027 El Niño event could further reduce precipitation and runoff during the remainder of the wet season. The combination of these observed deficits and the forecast of a potentially severe 2026-2027 El Niño event raises concerns regarding water availability during the upcoming 2027 dry season (January to April). These conditions require vigilant monitoring and prudent water resource management to always ensure the reliable and sustainable operation of the Canal. Particularly during the 2023-2024 El Niño event, the Canal maintained full open and timely communications with agents, owners and operators on the existing hydrological conditions of the waterway, a practice that we maintain at all times regardless of its criticality, as these hydrological conditions, is an essential aspect of our mutual interest. The measures described below are therefore being implemented to preserve service reliability, safeguard water resources for human consumption, and provide customers with timely and transparent information to support voyage planning and supply chain decisions. Effective August 21, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 4, 2026, the number of daily slots available at the Neopanamax Locks will be adjusted to nine (9). Accordingly, only one (1) slot will be offered during Booking Period 2. Additionally, the number of daily slots available at the Panamax Locks will be adjusted to twenty-five (25). Accordingly, only one (1) slot will be offered to Regular vessels during Booking Period 2. Due to the reduction in available transit slots during Booking Period 2, Conditioned slot in the Neopanamax category will not be available.

TO: All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT: Transit Reservation (Booking) System - Rule modifications The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) continues to experience climatic disruptions due to the current El Niño event, which is causing below-average rainfall and reduced water inflows to its reservoirs. To help ensure reliable Canal operations and preserve the draft available to customers, the ACP is introducing temporary modifications to the Transit Reservation (Booking) System. These changes are intended to allocate slots in the most equitable manner as possible, across market segments and prioritize vessels that make more efficient use of water. The following measures will take effect on the dates indicated below. Auctions methodology Given the current climate conditions and to promote a more equitable allocation process, considering market composition, including cargo type, market segment characteristics, and vessel operating models, the ACP will temporarily make selected auction slots available by market segment group. Similarly to what was temporarily implemented on November 29, 2023, this method aims to provide additional opportunities for different market segment vessels. Effective August 21, 2026, for booking dates beginning September 4, 2026, auction slots designated for Neopanamax, Super and Regular vessels may be made available to vessels within specific market segments, organized into groups, as shown in the following table: Group 1 Group 2 Group 3 Group 4 • Liquified Natural Gas • Liquified Petroleum Gas • Dry Bulk • General Cargo • Others • Full Container • Vehicle Carriers / RoRo • Refrigerated • Chemical Tankers • Crude/Product Tankers
The ACP will announce the day of the week on which the auction slot will be made available to each group. The specific dates on which the groups (one or more) identified above may participate in the auctions will be determined based on the number of vessels awaiting transit within each group and will be communicated through the Projected Booking Slots Availability table, published daily. Slot allocation Similarly to what was temporarily implemented on December 15, 2023, this method aims to provide additional opportunities for different customers, only one booking slot will be allowed per customer per day during the competition as shown in the following table:

For LoTSA program customers, deferrals and advanced services may be also limited under the current circumstances. 2. The Last-Minute service will be suspended until further notice. Furthermore, forfeited vessels must obtain a new slot to reschedule their transit.

Panama Canal Authority Vice Presidency for Operations Advisory To Shipping No. A-27-2026 August 14, 2026 TO : All Shipping Agents, Owners, and Operators SUBJECT : Underway Transfers of Provisions and Crew Changes in Pacific Canal Waters The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) reminds customers that all activities conducted within Panama Canal waters are subject to the Regulation on Navigation in Panama Canal Waters and require prior ACP authorization. Activities not expressly authorized by the ACP that may impede, delay, obstruct, or create risk to navigation, vessel operations, or lock operations are prohibited. Effective as instructed by the ACP, delivery of provisions, spare parts, equipment, or similar supplies, as well as crew changes, shall not be conducted underway in the Pacific navigation channel, including vessels proceeding southbound after departing Miraflores Locks or Cocoli Locks toward Diablo, unless specifically authorized by the ACP for exceptional operational or emergency reasons. These activities must be completed at authorized Pacific anchorage areas or other safe locations designated by the ACP before the beginning of transit, or as otherwise directed by the Authority. Masters, agents, operators, owners, vessel representatives, and launch companies shall plan and coordinate services accordingly before the vessel is underway to transit. This measure is intended to enhance safety of navigation and operational efficiency. Recent cases involving large pallets of provisions and crew changes with multiple persons and considerable baggage have contributed to prolonged movements between Miraflores and Diablo, particularly at night or during the early morning. Such conditions may increase risk during the transfer of personnel or supplies, expose launch crews and vessels to unnecessary hazards, and affect the scheduled positioning of the first Neopanamax transits in the Pacific Channel, including those subject to clear channel restrictions. The ACP will continue to evaluate Atlantic-side operations according to local anchorage limitations, traffic conditions, and prevailing weather or sea conditions outside the breakwater. Any service in Atlantic Canal waters shall be conducted only when and where specifically authorized by the ACP. Failure to comply with ACP instructions may result in administrative sanctions and liability for any costs, damages, delays, or operational impacts resulting from unauthorized activities. For additional information, please consult the Maritime Regulations available at https://pancanal.com/en/maritime-services/maritime- regulations/. For further information or assistance, please contact us at operationservices@pancanal.com. ORIGINAL SIGNED Boris Moreno Vásquez Vice President for Operations 3654-A (OP-I) V. 29/03/2023

VESSELS DRAGGING ANCHORS DUE TO GUSTY WINDS
1 Recently, there were reports of vessels dragging their anchors due to gusty winds with widespread showers arising from inter-monsoon disturbance over Singapore and the surrounding region.
2 Shipmaster and persons in charge of vessels at anchor in port are reminded to maintain a continuous navigational watch and be prepared for sudden onset of gusty winds during a thunderstorm. The preparation should include putting the ships’ engine on standby and paying out more cables if necessary in the prevailing circumstances. Please refer to Port Marine Circular No. 2 of 2007 on measures to be observed by vessels at anchor in port (http://www.mpa.gov.sg/circulars_and_notices/pdfs/pc07-02.pdf ).

Dynamic Shipping Zones A, B, C, D, and E: No restriction in effect.

SUEZ CANAL AUTHORITY PERIODICAL NO. (16/2026) ON 7-6-2026
Regarding the amendment of Circular No. (1/2022) Concerning (Laden/Ballast) “Crude Oil Tankers” [Rate (1) of the Transit Dues Schedule] passing the Suez Canal in both directions
Article One:
1) The surcharge levied on Laden “Crude Oil Tankers” [Rate (1L) of the Transit Dues Schedule] transiting the Suez Canal in both directions, is amended to be 37% of the Suez Canal normal transit dues rather than 25%.
2) The surcharge levied on ballast “Crude Oil Tankers” [Rate (1B) of the Transit Dues Schedule] transiting the Suez Canal in both directions, is amended to be 27% of the Suez Canal normal transit dues rather than 15%.
Noting that these surcharges are temporary and can be either amended or cancelled according to the “Maritime Industry” market conditions.
Article Two:
- This periodical is applicable to tankers transiting the Suez Canal from the 15th of July 2026.
.

SUEZ CANAL AUTHORITY CIRCULAR NO. (2/2026) ON 7-6-2026
Concerning (Laden/Ballast) “Containerships” [Rate (7) of the Transit Dues Schedule] transiting the Suez Canal in both directions
Article One:
(Laden/Ballast) “Containerships” [Rate (7) of the Transit Dues Schedule] transiting the Suez Canal in both directions will be charged with a surcharge of 12% from total Suez Canal transit dues (including normal transit dues in addition to surcharges for tiers of containers on weather deck).
Noting that these surcharges are temporary and can be either amended or cancelled according to the “Maritime Industry” market conditions.
Article Two:
- This circular is applicable to vessels transiting the Suez Canal from the 15th of July 2026.
.

w.t:
SECTOR ANCHORAGE, TERRITORIAL SEA - SECTOR ANCHORAGE, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA)
General / Hazards To Navigation / Obstructions
ConocoPhillips Alaska, Inc. (CPAI) plans to conduct marine ocean and seabed characterization studies near Oliktok Point. Studies will include buoy installation, tide gauge installation, bathymetric surveys, and navigational hazard surveys during the open water seasons of 2024, 2025, 2026, and 2027. Temporary monitoring equipment will be placed in the area to support the studies. This request is specific to activities planned for the 2026 season; an LMN will be submitted in subsequent years as needed. Buoy installation includes the deployment and recovery of three wave buoys offshore of Oliktok Point during the 2026 open water season. Preliminary buoy locations are included in Table 1 and shown on the attached map; final buoy locations may vary by about 1 nautical mile from the preliminary locations based on planning with local vessel operators and conditions encountered in the field. Buoy 1 will be installed in shallow water, approximately 5 to 10 feet deep. Buoys 2 and 3 will be installed in deeper water, approximately 25 to 30 feet deep. All buoys will float on the surface. Final buoy locations, depths, and water depth will be recorded and submitted within two days of deployment. Each Spotter buoy will be moored to the seafloor and will have a spar buoy equipped with an LED strobe light to alert mariners. Buoys will be deployed in late-July or early- August and recovered in late-September to mid-October. One tide gauge will be installed at or near the Oliktok Point during the 2026 open water season. The tide gauge will consist of a pressure transducer located in a water depth of three to five feet, a cable to shore, and a data recorder onshore. The pressure transducer will be located about 20 feet from shore and will be mounted on a ¾ inch pipe that sticks up above the water approximately 3 feet. The pipe will be driven 2 to 3 feet into the seabed using a post drive and will be clearly marked for safety. The onshore data recorder will be kept in a weather resistant container (e.g. cooler or bucket) and secured to the gravel bag jetty on the west side of Oliktok Point. A survey staff will be installed next to the pressure transducer to provide manual readout. The staff will also be attached to a ¾ inch pipe driven into the seabed in the same manner as the pressure transducer. The tide gauge will be installed at the beginning of the open-water season. The tide gauge and associated materials will be removed prior to freeze up. The stake on which the tide gauge is mounted could present a hazard for small boats transiting near the beach. Mariners should reduce wake when transiting the area and maintain a distance of at least 100 feet from the stake in the water and the data recorder on shore. Work is planned to begin as early as July 10, 2026. Please contact Miranda Buckmaster at (907) 263-4868 or miranda.buckmaster@conocophillips.com should you have any questions or require additional information.

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Arctic District (D17) LNM17-1B611E
w.t:
SECTOR ANCHORAGE, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA) - PRINCE WILLIAM SOUND
General / Hazards To Navigation / Hazards
Location: 61-10.32N 148-28.50W 61-10.24N 148-03.45W 61-02.28N 148-03.45W 60-55.81N 148-28.99W 61-10.32N 148-28.50W The State of Alaka is issuing routine updates on the Barry Arm Landslide Tsunami risk. This threat is located in Barry Arm and has the potential to create a tsunami if/when a landslide is generated that impacts the water in Barry Arm. If/when this occurs localized wave heights will be very hazardous in Barry Arm and Harriman Fjord. Port Wells and Passage Canal will also see inundation and strong, unusual currents for hours following an event. The geologic makeup of the area is similar to Alaskan locations where two previous landslide caused tsunamis occurred, in Lituya Bay (1958) and Icy Bay (2015), both causing extremely large but localized tsunamis. Mariners should maintain vigilance when in the vicinity of Barry Arm or nearby waters and be prepared to depart the area if any unusual geologic activity is observed. Studies are being conducted and the situation is being monitored to allow for a better understanding of the potential results of a slide. Additional information is available at https://dggs.alaska.gov/hazards/barry-arm-landslide.html.
Valid 2024-10-28 to 2029-10-27.

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM East District (D5) LNM05-41A6C0
w.t:
CAPE MAY INLET - NEW JERSEY INTRACOASTAL WATERWAY
General / Bridges / Maintenance
Location: 38-59.46N 074-50.00W Bridge Name: 47 State Route Bridge Mariners are advised that an engineering firm, on behalf of New Jersey Department of Transportation, will continue to be performing maintenance on the highway drawbridge 47 State Route (George Redding) Bridge, across the New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway (NJICW), Grassy Sound Channel, mile 108.9, at Wildwood, NJ. The maintenance which began in September 2026, will continue to be conducted from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Monday-Friday; through March 31, 2027. A 40-foot work barge and a tugboat will continue to be located in and around the vicinity of the bridge. During the work hours, the work barge will continue to be located within the entirety of the navigation channel of the bridge to provide access for structural steel repairs to the bascule span. Vessels may continue to safely transit through the bridge, if at least a one-hour prior notice is given to the project foreman. Maintenance personnel, equipment and vessels will continue to relocate from the moveable span and navigable channel, upon request. Work vessels may continue to be reached on VHF-FM channel 13 and 16. The project foreman can continue to be reached at (609) 579-8147. Mariners should use extreme caution navigating through the area. During the maintenance period, the bridge will be maintained in the closed-to-navigation position to perform structural steel repairs to the bridge bascule span. The bridge will remain in the closed-to-navigation position from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday through Thursday, and from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Friday, from January 4, 2027, through February 26, 2027. The bridge will not be able to open for emergencies. There is no immediate alternative route for vessels unable to pass through the bridge in the closed position. Vessels able to pass through the bridge in the closed position may do so at any time. At all other times, the drawbridge will operate in accordance with the operating regulations set out in Title 33 Code of Federal Regulations Part 117.5. Mariners should adjust their transits accordingly and should use caution when transiting the area. MSI #52664
Valid 2026-11-23 to 2027-04-09.

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM East District (D5) LNM05-DC5ADB
w.t:
SECTOR DELAWARE BAY, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA) - CAPE MAY INLET
General / Bridges / Proposal
Location: 38-57.35N 074-52.45W Bridge Name: 621 County Route Bridge All interested parties are notified that the Commander, Coast Guard East District has received a proposal from the Cape May County Bridge Commission with plans for replacement of an existing highway drawbridge across a navigable waterway of the United States. WATERWAY AND LOCATION: Middle Thorofare, New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway (NJICW), at mile 112.2, at approximate location [38-57.35N 074-52.45W], and the Upper Thorofare, at mile 0.0, at approximate location [38-57.32N 074-52.62W] near Lower Township, Cape May County, NJ. CHARACTER OF WORK: The proposed project is to replace the Two-Mile drawbridge, located on County Route 621 (Ocean Drive), across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, with a fixed bridge that will carry County Route 621 (Ocean Drive), across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, and Upper Thorofare, near Lower Township, Cape May County, NJ. The purpose of the project is to address structural, geometric, carrying capacity, and operational deficiencies of the Cape May County Bridge Commission-owned bridge located across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, on the Ocean Drive Causeway, and to provide safe, efficient, and reliable passage for all modes of transportation. The existing drawbridge across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, has a horizontal clearance of 50.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 23.00 feet above mean high water in the closed position and unlimited vertical clearance in the open position. The replacement bridge will be a fixed bridge across Middle Thorofare, NJICW, and Upper Thorofare. The portion of the replacement bridge across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, will provide a horizontal clearance of 80.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 80.00 feet above mean high water. The portion of the replacement bridge across Upper Thorofare, will provide a horizontal clearance of 50.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 49.73 feet above mean high water. A copy of Preliminary Public Notice D05PPN-06-2026, which describes the proposal in detail, can be obtained by calling (571) 607-6762 or by viewing at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/public-notice-for-bridges-active (select East District). Comments will be received for the record at the address in the header or via email at (D5Portsmouth-BridgesPublicNotice@uscg.mil) no later than December 4, 2026.
Valid 2026-11-04 to 2026-12-05.
USCG East District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

Mobile Channel - Safety Zone/Naval Protection Zone --- On: 2026-11-11 --- The U.S. Coast Guard, State, and local law enforcement will enforce a Naval Protection Zone and a Safety Zone on navigable waters within the Captain of the Port Mobile area for the arrival of the M/V EX ENTERPRISE, expected on or about November 11, 2026, until the vessel is towed to its final mooring on the Mobile River. The Safety Zone will include all navigable waters within the Mobile Bar Channel, beginning at Mobile Bar Lighted Buoy 1 (LLNR-6100), northward through the boundaries of the Mobile River Channel, ending at the Cochrane Bridge. This zone will be enforced to prevent meeting situations with the M/V EX ENTERPRISE during the dead-ship tow. Portions of the Safety Zone intersecting the GIWW or other intersections with Federal Channels will be enforced to the extent necessary to prevent meeting situations during the transit and are not expected to be enforced after the M/V EX ENTERPRISE and all vessels involved in the towing operation clear the intersection. The Naval Protection Zone will include a 500-yard zone around the vessel and will be enforced from the vessel’s entry into the COTP Mobile Zone until the vessel is safely moored on the Mobile River. No person or vessel may enter or remain in the zone unless authorized by the COTP or a designated representative. No vessel or person may enter within 100-yards without authorization. Vessels within 500-yards must operate at the minimum speed necessary to maintain a safe course. To seek permission to enter these zones, mariners can contact the COTP or the COTP’s representative on VHF-FM Channel 16 during the enforcement period. Those authorized transit within the zones, must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative. Concerned parties should contact the U. S. Coast Guard Sector Mobile Command Center at (251) 266-5888 or on VHF-FM Channel 16.

MOBILE CHANNEL - MOBILE RIVER
General / LAA / RNA / Safety Zone
Mobile River Channel - Safety Zone ---  To: May 2030 --- The Captain of the Port (COTP) Mobile is enforcing a fixed Safety Zone in accordance with 33 CFR 165.T08-1214 surrounding the M/V EX ENTERPRISE as the vessel is moored at a receiving facility located on the Mobile River at 701 South Royal Street, Mobile, AL. This Safety Zone is necessary to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from hazards associated with a dismantling operation, including removal of hazardous and regulated materials, and continuous work activity on and around the hull. All navigable waters of the Mobile River along the RDB will be designated as a fixed moored Safety Zone and will be bound by the following coordinates: 30-40.57N 088-02.27W, 30-40.57N 088-02.22W, 30-40.30N 088-02.08W, 30-40.32N 088-02.27W and north along the shoreline to the point of origin. The Safety Zone does not include waters within the Mobile River Federal Channel; therefore, no impact to commercial vessel traffic is anticipated. This zone will be enforced for the duration of dismantling operations, and remain in effect until the COTP determines the area no longer presents safety concerns. The dismantlement project is expected to progress to a safe stage approximately May 2030. In the event this fixed moored Safety Zone is no longer needed before May 2030, mariners will be notified through a Marine Safety Information Bulletin (MSIB) or other appropriate means. No person may enter or remain in the zone unless authorized by the COTP or a designated representative. Those in the Safety Zone must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative. To seek permission to enter, mariners can contact the COTP or the COTP’s representative on VHF-FM Channel 16.
Valid 2026-11-09 until further notice.
USCG Heartland (Gulf) District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

General / Miscellaneous
Alabama River - In accordance with Section 7-11 of the ACT Master Water Control Manual dated April 2022, full navigation channel availability on the Alabama River is dependent upon channel maintenance, seasonal flow conditions, and basin status. Flows for navigation are most needed in the unregulated portion of the lower Alabama River below Claiborne Lock and Dam. Alabama Power Company (APC) operates its reservoirs on the Coosa and Tallapoosa Rivers to provide a minimum navigation flow target in the Alabama River at Montgomery, Alabama. Basin status criteria are correlated to APC Drought Operations (ADROP) updates which monitors drought triggers related to basin inflow, state line flow on the Coosa River between Georgia and Alabama, as well as composite storage availability within the APC projects. These updates are provided monthly on the first and third Tuesday. Below is the most recent ADROP update provided by Alabama Power Company on October 20, 2026: *ADROP UPDATE* - Low Basin Inflow: FALSE - - Low State Line Flow: FALSE - - Low Composite Storage: FALSE - - Montgomery Flow Target: 4,200 cfs daily average (NOTE: ADROP requires one drought intensity level change per cycle regardless of the number of triggers enacted when exiting drought operations.) - - Current Operations: Drought Intensity Level 1 - Currently, based on profile survey conducted on 04JUN2024, a 10 ft tailwater elevation near Claiborne Lock is required to provide a 9 ft navigation channel on the lower Alabama River. A modified depth of 7.5 ft navigable draft can be provided with a tailwater elevation of 8.5 ft at the Claiborne Lock and Dam. Commercial mariners should check water levels daily and schedule lockage appointments by calling the Claiborne Lock Supervisor at (251) 282-4575. Tailwater elevations below Claiborne Lock and Dam can be viewed at: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-02428401
Position 31-36.90N 087-33.10W

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Heartland District Rivers (D8) LNM08R-DDBB32
w.t:
NEW ORLEANS TO BATON ROUGE - LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER
General / MSIB
The U.S. Coast Guard COTP Lower Mississippi River has issued a low water Safety Advisory between approximate Miles 869.0 and 303.0. The USACE maintained depths and widths, may not be attainable on all buoy lines. It is recommended that mariners monitor all gauge readings for safe navigation. The U.S. Coast Guard COTP Lower Mississippi River, with the concurrence of the Lower Mississippi River Committee, recommends the following limits for tows: Southbound tows between Miles 869.0 and 585.0 Drafts no greater than 11.6 feet. Barges to be configured no more than 7 wide. Southbound tows between Miles 585.0 and 303.0 Drafts no greater than 12.6 feet. Barges to be configured no more than 7 wide. Northbound tows between Miles 869.0 and 303.0 Drafts no greater than 10.6 feet. Barges to be configured no more than 6 wide total, and loaded barges no more than 4 wide. Barges to be configured no more than 7 long. Barges currently in the system with drafts greater than the advised depths should be placed as near to the center of the tow as possible. Mariners are requested to contact U.S. Coast Guard Western Rivers Command Center via VHF-FM Channel 16 or at (866) 777-2784, to report areas of shoaling, hazardous conditions or missing aids to navigation.
Position 36-20.10N 089-32.98W

w.t:
LONG ISLAND SOUND EASTERN PART - NEW HAVEN HARBOR
General / MSIB
Location: 41-16.93N 072-54.93W SUMMARY: The U.S. Anny Corps of Engineers (USACE). New England District, will be conducting dredging operations in support of the New Haven Harbor Improvement Project in New Haven, Connecticut. Mariners are advised to use caution, maintain a proper lookout. and communicate early with the dredging vessel when operating in or near the project area. SITUATION: The New Haven Harbor Improvement Project will modernize approximately 5.5 miles of the federal navigation channel serving the deep-water terminals of New Haven. Great Lakes Dock and Dredge Company, under contract with USACE, is expected to conduct work over two dredging cycles. The first one beginning in October 2026 and continuing through March 2027, and the second cycle beginning in October 2027 and continuing through March 2028. Operations are planned to take place 24 hours a clay, 7 days a week. Planned improvements include deepening the entrance channel, main channel, maneuvering area, and turning basin from 35 feet to 40 feet; widening the entrance channel from 500 feet to 600 feet outside the breakwaters; widening the channel bend between the breakwaters from 560 feet to 800 feet; widening the main channel inside the harbor from 400 feet to 500 feet; and optimizing the turning basin for larger vessels. Dredging operations may affect normal vessel movement, maneuvering, and transit within New Haven Harbor. Mariners should anticipate the presence of dredging equipment and associated support vessels within the federal navigation channel and surrounding work areas. Vessels looking to transit the area are urged to contact the dredge early to arrange safe passage and to maintain a proper lookout when navigating near operations. COMMUNICATIONS: For urgent safety-of-life matters, please contact the Sector Long Island Sound Command Center on VHF-FM Channel 16 or call (866) 299-8031. Working Vessels will monitor channels 13, 16, and 79. Additionally, please check USCG Navigation Center oflen for updates to the public from the US Coast Guard. Questions regarding this bulletin may be directed to Lieutenant Joel Chapman. ChiefofWaterways Management Division at (475) 355-5336 or email SECLlSSPWMarineEvent@uscg.mil.
Valid 2026-10-26 to 2027-04-01.

WASHINGTON – LAKE WASHINGTON SHIP CANAL – Montlake Bridge deviation notice The Coast Guard intends to approve a temporary deviation from the normal operating schedule that governs the Montlake Street Bridge (BRDG UID 31183) across the Lake Washington Ship Canal, mile 5.2. The Montlake Street Bridge need not open the draw for marine vessels during heavy road traffic for the 2026 University of Washington football games on the following dates and times: - 06 Sep 1000 to 1330 and 1600 to 1830; - 12 Sep, 0930 to 1300 and 1530 to 1800; - 19 Sep, 1300 to 1700 and 1900 to 2200; - 26 Sep, 1700 to 2030 and 2300 to 0130; - 09 Oct, 1500 to 1830 and 2100 to 2330; - 07 Nov, 0930 to 1300 and 1530 to 1800; - 21 Nov, TBD. The deviation is necessary to accommodate vehicular traffic attending football games at Husky Stadium at the University of Washington, in Seattle, Washington. This deviation will allow Montlake Bridge to remain in the closed-to-navigation position before and after each game. Due to television scheduling, game times will be published at later dates when determined, and the MSI will be updated with the bridge closure times. Vessels which do not require a bridge opening may continue to transit beneath this bridge during the closure. The bridge will be required to open, if needed, for vessels engaged in emergency response operations during this closure period. The Coast Guard will publish any updates or changes to this operating schedule in future MSI announcements. The bridge shall operate in accordance with 33 CFR § 117.897 at all other times. If any mariner cannot support the dates listed for a bridge closure, please submit a comment by 04 Jul 2026 at SMB-CGD-NW-BRIDGES@USCG.MIL. w.t:
SALMONBAY
General / Bridges
WASHINGTON – LAKE WASHINGTON SHIP CANAL – SHILSHOLE BAY – Bridge notice (Revised) Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway Company (BNSF) will be performing heavy rail maintenance/construction on the Salmon Bay Railroad Bridge (BRDG UID 31177) (AKA BNSF Bridge 6.3), mile 0.1, across the Lake Washington Ship Canal in Seattle, Washington. The construction work requires the draw of the subject bridge to be closed from 02 November 2026 to 25 November 2026. This draw closure corresponds with the USACE’s large Hiram M. Chittenden Lock closure. The Coast Guard has approved a temporary deviation to the operating schedule that governs the Salmon Bay Railroad Bridge from 0600 on 02 November 2026 to 1600 on 25 November 2026. The draw will be able to open from 8 A.M. to 8 P.M on 14 - 18 November 2026, if a 24-hour notice is given to the bridge operator. The subject bridge provides 43 feet of vertical clearance in the closed-to-navigation position at mean higher high water. Vessels which do not require a bridge opening may continue to transit beneath the bridge during this closure period. This construction requires barges in the navigation channel during the same time as USACE’s annual lock closure and maintenance to minimize impacts. A crane and material barge will be positioned in the water to service the work of erecting temporary trusses that are required to execute the counterweight change out. During this timeframe, access on the southern channel to the small locks will be in operation during the large lock closure. A construction zone will be established for mariners to navigate around at minimum safe speed. The subject bridge will not be able to open for emergencies, and there is no immediate alternate route for vessels to pass. For more information on this draw bridge closure contact Travis Woodley at travis.woodley@bnsf.com or (682) 978-3311.

General / Bridges / Rehabilitation
Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT) and Carter Construction will be completing a cathodic protection project on the US-101 Bridge (BRDG UID 29514) (LLNR 9627) across the entrance to Depoe Bay, OR. The planned start time/date is 0600 on 5 Jan 2026 through 1800 on 18 Dec 2026. The start and end dates may change due to weather conditions. The work requires the use of containment via scaffolding, that will reduce the vertical navigation clearance of the subject bridge from 46 feet to 41 feet at high tide for the center horizontal 38ft above the main navigation channel. There will also be scaffolding that will hang about 19’ below the bottom of the bridge on the north and south side of the bridge arch of the main navigation channel and will remain in place until maintenance is completed until November / December. The containment will be marked with amber caution lighting and will not obstruct any navigational aids. For more information contact Markus Schaaf at Markus.Schaaf@odot.oregon.gov.

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Northwest District (D13) LNM13-7C8C66
w.t:
SECTOR COLUMBIA RIVER, EXCLUSIVE ECONOMIC ZONE (EEZ) - SECTOR COLUMBIA RIVER, TERRITORIAL SEA
General / Miscellaneous
PacWave continues to maintain a network of site monitoring equipment, seafloor instrumentation, and subsea cable infrastructure throughout the PacWave South wave energy test site, approximately 7 nautical miles WSW of the Yaquina Bay Entrance. Some of the monitoring buoys are low profile and may be difficult to see in elevated sea states. All buoys have a yellow hull, are lighted with a flashing amber light, and are deployed as single-point moorings. PacWave has also installed four long-term surface marker buoys that visually delineate the corners of the test site: NW (44°34.9988'N, 124°14.4998'W), NE (44°35.0465'N, 124°13.1008'W), SE (44°33.0437'N, 124°12.9700'W), and SW (44°33.0000'N, 124°14.3730'W). These corner markers are approximately 9 feet tall, have a yellow / red hull, a fixed yellow tower structure with integrated radar reflector, green grating on the lower half of the tower, reflective tape on the upper tower, and are lighted. These markers are also single-point moorings and will remain in place as part of PacWave’s maintained offshore infrastructure. Mariners should be aware that subsurface equipment and mooring components may also be present. Mariners are requested to avoid the test site if possible and to use caution when navigating in or near the area. For additional information, contact brett.hembrough@oregonstate.edu or 541-737-9023. If there is an emergency or concerns regarding this equipment, please call our 24 / 7 Watch Desk at 541-819-4096.
USCG Northwest District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

w.t:
STRAIT OF JUAN DE FUCA - ADMIRALTY INLET
General / Miscellaneous
MSIB 004-26 Quiet Sound Voluntary Slowdown https://www.pacificarea.uscg.mil/Our-Organization/Northwest-District/District-Staff/dp/dpw/notices/ The Quiet Sound voluntary commercial vessel slowdown in Admiralty Inlet aims to reduce underwater noise in Southern Resident killer whale critical habitat. The 2025-26 slowdown will be in effect starting at 0001 PST on 3 September 2026 and will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PST on 31 January 2027, at the latest, depending on orca presence. More information can be found at: https://quietsound.org/admiralty-inlet-slowdown. When in effect, the slowdown requests all inbound and outbound commercial vessels transiting through the slowdown zone not exceed the following speeds through water when safe and operationally feasible: 11 knots – General cargo, bulkers and tankers 14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels The voluntary vessel slowdown takes place in the inbound and outbound lanes of the shipping lanes within these boundaries: Northwest: a line drawn from Pt Hudson (48-07.04N 122-44.93W) to Admiralty Head (48-09.25N 122-40.77W) Northeast: a line drawn from Randall Pt (47-58.99N 122-21.17W) to Mukilteo Light (47-56.89N 122-18.48W) South: a line drawn from Apple Cove Pt (47-48-55.926N, 122-28.51.186W) to Edwards Pt (47-48.20N 122-23.70W) Speed transition zones are in place about 5 nautical miles prior to entering the slowdown area. Any directions from Puget Sound Vessel Traffic Service take precedence and supersede these measures. The voluntary slowdown is led by the Quiet Sound program at Maritime Blue, in cooperation with government agencies, tribal governments, industry partners and conservation groups. For more detailed information related to this slowdown and the Quiet Sound program, including a graphic of the voluntary slowdown area, refer to the following web address: https://quietsound.org/admiralty-inlet-slowdown.
USCG Northwest District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

General / Naval Activity / Naval Gunnery Exercises
Intermittent missile firing operations are conducted by the Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF), Barking Sands, Kauai, in the Whiskey 188 (W-188) operating area. Operations are conducted periodically throughout each week in an area bound by the following coordinates: 22:00N/159:51W, 22:00N/160:00W, 22:04N/160:06W, 21:59.5N/160:21W, 22:05N/161:35W, 22:45N/161:25W, 22:56N/161:49W, 23:34N/161:18.6W, 23:57N/160:41W, 25:41N/161:36W, 26:00N/159:58W, 25:47N/158:15W, 23:54N/158:15W, 22:20N/159:09W, 22:21N/159:30W, 22:13N/159:42W, 22:00N/159:51W Intermittent high power radar operations are conducted by PMRF at the following position: 22:03N/159:47W Request all mariners remain at least one mile off the coastline between Kokole Point and Nohili Point. Vessels may be requested to alter course due to firing operations and are requested to contact "Pacific Missile Range Facility" on VHF-Ch 16 prior to entering the above boundaries. If unable to contact the PMRF prior to entering or while in the warning area, relay messages through U.S. Coast Guard Honolulu. Vessels inbound and outbound for Hawaiian ports will create the least interference to firing operations as well as enhance vessel's safety by passing South of the Islands of Kauai and Niihau during the specified times. The work will be ongoing from on or about September 21, 2026, with an estimated completion date of February l, 2027 from Kings Bay Lighted Buoy 43 (LLNR 37735) to Kings Bay Light 60 (LLNR 7035). All mariners are requested to stay clear of the dredge, pipelines, barge, derricks and operating wires about the dredge. All operators should be aware that the dredge and pontoon lines are held in place by cables, which are attached to anchors some distance from the dredge and pontoons. Buoys are attached to the anchors so that they may be moved as the dredge moves. Submerged lines should be avoided. Mariners are requested to exercise extreme caution when approaching, passing, and leaving the dredging plant. The DREDGE NEWMARKET monitors VHF-FM channels 13 and 16. Mariners are cautioned to strictly comply with the Inland Rules of the Road when approaching, passing and leaving the area of operations, and remain a safe distance away from the dredge, booster, buoys, cables, pipeline, barges, derricks, wires and related equipment. Owners and lessees of fishnets, crabpots and other structures that may be in the vicinity and that may hinder the free navigation of attending vessels and equipment must remove these from the area where tugs, tenderboats and other attendant equipment will be navigating.
